findings.summary: The `## Open upgrade` IOU's load-bearing rule — 'deterministic-oracle evals are blocking CI gates; LLM-judge evals are tracked trend lines' — is too coarse to ship. The oracle being deterministic says nothing about its SUBJECT: 'did the agent refuse / select the right tool / get the count right' is stochastic however mechanically it is checked, so shipping the IOU verbatim would have installed a flaky gate in the same document that forbids them (§7).
findings.disposition: §5b splits on agent-path INDEPENDENCE rather than on oracle mechanism: invariants true regardless of what the agent chose may block; path-dependent outcomes run k/k over N with AMBER, reusing run_calibration's existing rule rather than minting a second. §5a's blocking oracles were re-read and turn out to be the same shape, which is the reason they can gate — a fact the IOU had mis-attributed to harness ownership.

findings.summary: The IOU had two live callers with no implementation behind them: §8's [→EVAL] tag routed prompt/tool-definition/agent-behavior changes to 'the open §-upgrade below', and §5a's MCP bullet forward-referenced 'the pending agent-eval upgrade'. A promise consumed by two surfaces and fulfilled by none.
findings.disposition: Both cross-references now resolve to §5b, and both are pinned as needles so a future edit cannot re-dangle them silently. A dedicated check asserts no pointer to the removed section survives anywhere in the file.

findings.summary: A single `eval` marker cannot express §5b, because the section defines two lanes with opposite gate semantics — one that may block and one that must never gate. Registering one marker would have left the trend lane indistinguishable from the blocking lane in any `pytest -m` audit.
findings.disposition: Two markers registered — `eval` (blocking lane, agent-path-INDEPENDENT invariants only) and `eval_judge` (trend lane, never gates) — mirroring the existing `ux`/`ux_probe` split, with the reason stated inline so the pair is not later 'simplified' back to one. Stated weakness: this repo has no pytest.ini, so the marker list is prose and nothing binds a marker to a real test.

findings.summary: The skill description had 6 characters of headroom against its 1024 budget and needed ~45 for eval trigger vocabulary. After a dedupe trim it sits at 1021 — 3 characters spare. The budget is now structurally exhausted: the next doctrine addition cannot buy trigger vocabulary by trimming, because the remaining text is no longer redundant.
findings.disposition: Trimmed by dedupe as David's standing rule requires (warn, never silently exceed, never cut trigger vocabulary): 'wiring-liveness discipline' lost a redundant word, the second 'audits' and the second 'grading' were dropped, and UX probes and agent evals were MERGED into one clause because they share one rule — which is a doctrinal improvement, not only a saving. A regression check confirms no trigger word was lost: only the hyphenated compounds 'agent-driven' and 'wiring-liveness' changed form, and both survive as their components. FLAGGED FOR DAVID rather than closed: 3 characters is not a budget, and the next addition needs a real restructure or a raised ceiling — a decision that is his, not an agent's.

findings.summary: tag_guard fired on a READ-ONLY tag listing used to resolve a baseline rev for check_scoreboard_integrity.py — it matches the verb substring and cannot distinguish enumerating tags from creating one. It then blocked the guard_note.py RECORD of that block, because the note quoted the offending command, so the §12 accounting mechanism is unusable for this gate unless the operator paraphrases.
findings.disposition: RECORDED, not worked around: guard_note.py record --gate tagguard, performed_elsewhere=yes, naming the substitution (the same read via a different porcelain) so it is distinguishable from evasion. Left OPEN because neither half is fixed. Reuses the existing recurrence key — this is the SECOND record of a guard treating an out-of-jurisdiction action as a violation, which by the ledger's own rule makes it an UNBUILT GUARD candidate the next recurrence report will surface. Neither half is a release-path risk; both are adoption risks, and a guard that blocks reads is exactly how an operator learns to reach for the demotion switch.

findings.summary: §5b's reference implementation does not travel: install_into_repo.py vendors no calibration/, so a downstream repo adopting §5b gets doctrine describing a harness it does not have. Every other blocking-capable discipline in the Playbook ships an instrument (§2→/edge, §4→/mutate, §5a→/probe, §6→/tripwire, §12→/claims).
findings.rationale: Rejected as a defect and STATED as a limit instead. Building a /eval command plus an eval-calibrator agent would duplicate calibration/ — the architecture-adversary confirmed the rejection as correct, and a parallel surface would be textbook DUPLICATION plus GATE-BY-PROXY. §5b therefore says in its own body that downstream it is BYO-harness and that calibration/ is a reference implementation rather than a shipped tool, so the reader is never told to run something that is not there. Making the gap loud in the doctrine is the honest close; hiding it behind a thin command would not be.
